newsitem.title: JAMAICA: CRICKET-BISHOP DOUBTFUL FOR SECOND TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BISHOP DOUBTFUL FOR SECOND TEST.

text.p: West Indies fast bowler Ian Bishop is fighting to overcome a hamstring strain in time to play in the second test against India which starts on Friday in Port of Spain.

Bishop left the field on the last day of the drawn first test on Monday without bowling a ball in India's second innings because of what West Indies team manager Clive Lloyd described as "a slight tightness of the hamstring".
The 30-year-old Trinidadian bowled well for figures of three for 62 in the first innings and would dearly love to perform for his home fans.
Fellow Trinidadian Mervyn Dillon has been named as standby.

West Indies captain Courtney Walsh said the injury was not serious. "He had a slight stiffness in his hamstring," said Walsh. "I told him to come out and move around in case we got a couple of wickets (and there was a need for him to bowl).
"We did not get the early wickets we expected so we decided it would not have cost us much to send him off to get some treatment."
